prompt: What was state of the schools regarding integration in the hometown of Miller Williams when he began his master's degree in Zoology?
answer:
When Miller Williams began graduate study in zoology—around 1951–52—his hometown of Hoxie, Arkansas, still operated a racially segregated public-school system. Black and white children attended separate schools, as was customary and legally enforced in Arkansas at the time.

Hoxie did not begin desegregating its schools until 1955, making it one of the earliest Arkansas districts to do so after *Brown v. Board of Education* (1954). The move provoked substantial local opposition and litigation, but the schools ultimately opened on an integrated basis in 1955.
